cases.prompt: How many customers are there?

check.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

cases.prompt: How many customers are there in each country? Show the country and the count.

check.reference_sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY country

cases.prompt: Which customer signed up most recently? Give just their name.

check.reference_sql: SELECT name FROM customers ORDER BY signup_date DESC LIMIT 1

cases.prompt: Which customers have never placed an order? Give just their names.

check.reference_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)

cases.prompt: How many orders have been paid?

check.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'

cases.prompt: Which customers have placed more than one order, counting every status? Give just their names.

check.reference_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

cases.prompt: What is the total revenue, in cents, from paid orders?

check.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid'

cases.prompt: How much money, in cents, was refunded?

check.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'refunded'

cases.prompt: What is the total revenue, in cents, from paid orders placed by customers in the USA?

check.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND c.country = 'USA'

cases.prompt: What is the revenue, in cents, from paid orders for each product category? Show the category and the revenue.

check.reference_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.category

cases.prompt: Which customer has spent the most on paid orders? Give just their name.

check.reference_sql: SELECT c.name FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.prompt: What are the top 3 products by revenue from paid orders? Give just their names, highest revenue first.

check.reference_sql: SELECT p.name FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) DESC, p.name LIMIT 3

cases.prompt: How many orders were placed in each month? Show the month as YYYY-MM and the count, oldest month first.

check.reference_sql: SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

cases.prompt: For each month that has paid orders, show the month as YYYY-MM, that month's paid revenue in cents, and the running total of paid revenue up to and including that month. Oldest month first.

check.reference_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT substr(o.order_date, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) FROM monthly ORDER BY month

cases.prompt: For each month with paid orders except the first, show the month as YYYY-MM and how much paid revenue changed from the month before, in cents (negative if it went down). Oldest month first.

check.reference_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT substr(o.order_date, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY month), changes AS (SELECT month, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change FROM monthly) SELECT month, change FROM changes WHERE change IS NOT NULL ORDER BY month

cases.prompt: What share of paid revenue does each product category bring in? Show the category and its percentage of the total, rounded to one decimal place.

check.reference_sql: WITH by_category AS (SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.category) SELECT category, ROUND(100.0 * revenue / (SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM by_category), 1) FROM by_category

cases.prompt: What is the average value of a paid order in each country, in cents? Show the country and the average.

check.reference_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT o.id, c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.id) SELECT country, AVG(total) FROM totals GROUP BY country

cases.prompt: Which paid orders are worth more than the average paid order? Show the order id and its value in cents.

check.reference_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT o.id, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.id) SELECT id, total FROM totals WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM totals)

cases.prompt: What is the median value of a paid order, in cents? When there is an even number of orders, the median is the average of the two middle values.

check.reference_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT o.id, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.id), ranked AS (SELECT total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total) AS n, COUNT(*) OVER () AS count FROM totals) SELECT AVG(total) FROM ranked WHERE n IN ((count + 1) / 2, (count + 2) / 2)

cases.prompt: For each product category, which product brought in the most paid revenue? Show the category, the product name and that revenue in cents.

check.reference_sql: WITH revenue AS (SELECT p.category, p.name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.id), ranked AS (SELECT category, name, revenue, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS place FROM revenue) SELECT category, name, revenue FROM ranked WHERE place = 1

cases.prompt: Which customers have bought every product in the stationery category, counting only paid orders? Give just their names.

check.reference_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND p.category = 'stationery' GROUP BY c.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = 'stationery')

cases.prompt: For each customer with at least two orders of any status, show their name and the date of their second order.

check.reference_sql: WITH numbered AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS n FROM orders) SELECT c.name, numbered.order_date FROM numbered JOIN customers c ON c.id = numbered.customer_id WHERE numbered.n = 2

cases.prompt: For each signup month (YYYY-MM), show how many customers signed up and how many of them made a paid order within 14 days of signing up (day 14 counts). Oldest month first.

check.reference_sql: WITH quick AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND julianday(o.order_date) - julianday(c.signup_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 14) SELECT substr(c.signup_date, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*), COUNT(quick.id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN quick ON quick.id = c.id GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

cases.prompt: Which customers spent more on paid orders than the average spend of the paying customers in their own country? Give just their names.

check.reference_sql: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price_cents) AS spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY c.id) SELECT name FROM spend AS s WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM spend WHERE country = s.country)
